questions.text: Which mapping best matches MCP primitives to consumer intent in this lesson?

options.A: Tool: read a URI; resource: start a template; prompt: mutate state.
options.B: Tool: start a template; resource: mutate state; prompt: read a URI.
options.C: Tool: perform an operation; resource: read URI-addressed content; prompt: start a user-selected message workflow.
options.D: Tool: store policy; resource: override host instructions; prompt: authorize operations.

questions.explanation: Tools expose operations, resources expose addressable content, and prompts package reusable message workflows chosen by users.

questions.text: A client receives a resource-updated notification for notes://note-1. What should it do to obtain the current content?

options.A: Read the URI again through resources/read under current authorization.
options.B: Treat the notification as the complete replacement document.
options.C: Reuse the subscription ID as proof of permission to read the note.
options.D: Assume all cached note bodies now contain the updated text.

questions.explanation: An update notification identifies changed content; the client must read it again and remain subject to current authorization.

questions.text: A SubscriptionStream has notifications={"resourcesListChanged": True} and no resourceSubscriptions entry. What does resource_updated("notes://note-1") return?

options.A: An update event because any resource-related subscription allows it.
options.B: A complete result that includes the note body.
options.C: A JSON-RPC error with code -32602 for the absent URI filter.
options.D: None because that URI is not in resourceSubscriptions.

questions.explanation: resource_updated checks membership in resourceSubscriptions, defaulting to an empty list. resourcesListChanged enables a separate notification category.
